A good cult classic.

If you’re looking for a game that captures the "no-nonsense" spirit of old-school shooters like Quake or Painkiller, Hard Reset Redux delivers a satisfying, neon-drenched punch to the face. It’s a visually striking cyberpunk romp that prioritizes big guns and even bigger explosions. However, while the chrome shines bright, a few dents in the armor keep it from being a total masterpiece.

The Good:
 The standout feature is undoubtedly the combat flow. The weapon system is unique; rather than carrying twenty individual guns, you have two modular bases (the CLN Firearm and the NRG Weapon) that transform into various death-dealing gadgets. Swapping between a mortar launcher and a railgun on the fly feels incredibly fluid.
 Atmosphere: The rain-slicked, futuristic streets are dripping with style.
 Performance: The Redux version runs like a dream, handling massive waves of robots without breaking a sweat.
 Cyber-Upgrades: The progression system is rewarding, making you feel like a walking tank by the final act.

The Bad: 
 While the game encourages you to blow everything up, it inadvertently creates one of its most frustrating nuisances. Collectibles and gear pickups are physically simulated. In a game where every room is packed with explosive barrels and volatile machinery, one stray shot often sends your precious NANO upgrade canisters flying into unreachable corners or hiding behind piles of physics-based debris. Spending five minutes playing "find the needle in the haystack" after a high-intensity firefight really kills the momentum.

The Ugly:
 The game’s biggest hurdle is its repetitive nature.
 Enemy Variety: You’ll be fighting the same swarms of "gorilla-bots" and small "saw-drones" for the majority of the campaign.
 Level Design: While the aesthetic is gorgeous, the actual pathfinding boils down to: enter arena, kill everything, find a battery to open a door, repeat.

Final Verdict
 Hard Reset Redux is a solid 6.5/10. It is a fantastic choice if you want to turn your brain off and enjoy some high-fidelity destruction. It’s crunchy, fast, and unapologetically difficult. Just be prepared for the gameplay loop to wear a bit thin before the credits roll, and try not to blast your upgrades into orbit.

This is the third game I’ve played from that developer (the first ones being Evil West and Shadow Warrior), and it's probably the most fun one overall. Mostly because this one doesn’t overstay its welcome to the absolute breaking point. It just starts, shows us some gorgeous cyberpunk levels, allows us to murder some robots for a while, and then promptly ends.

It is absolutely nothing special: the combat loop is just a little more involved than something like Serious Sam, the story feels like it was written by ChatGPT, and all the bosses actually do overstay their welcome like crazy - but it’s still a perfect second-screen game to listen to podcasts with. Nothing less, nothing more.

+ graphics are nice
+ can run on a potato (my 1L mini pc ran 30 FPS @ 720p)

... but everything else is ... "meh" to "ugh"

- the "gritty night city" dark color pallete has everything blending together

I started this game with a "this is interesting" attitude, but as the game progressed I just wanted to get it over with. You fight through a wave of enemies, then wander around trying to figure out where to go. You know you're on the right track when another wave of enemies is unleashed. There's nothing organic about it. It's as if all the enemies are lined up at starting gates for the kentucky derby, and you crossing certain lines in the game unleashes them. Then you wander around more, next wave shows up.

This becomes repetitious and quite distracting after a while. B/c other games will more organically place enemies. They'll have a few in a hallway. They'll have a big lug in some room when you round a corner. You'll encounter them in a more organic, hand-placed way.

The way enemies come across in Hard Reset, it absolutely feels like you just trigger "spawn enemies" areas, and the enemies just spawn in. They're not already there organically. This makes it easier to make easy, med, hard modes I guess, b/c you just up the spawn count in the trigger. But, it creates this repetitious "waves" fighting pattern. Go some place, trigger a "wave", fight it, move on. It just becomes a slog after a while.

And, while there's lots of weapon types, there's no real indication if certain weapons do better against certain enemies. You have really big hulking lugs. Shotgun, grenade, rockets.. it all seems to just do the same to them. Sometimes they go down easily. Other times they take a beating like a bullet sponge. I guess the enemies spawn with random health? I never got to a point where I went "ah, THIS enemy, I know exactly how to deal with them!" Nope. I was just pulling out random weapons and blasting away until out of ammo, then switched weapons.

The main perk of some weapons is they can paralyze or ensnare enemies. This lets you switch to another weapon to blast them easier. But, for the most part, the weapons all "work" the same in that they don't seem to make a difference. So, you just pick if you want to machine gun, shotgun, pulse rifle, shock mortar, etc the enemies how you see fit. A lot of the combat is just enemy management to avoid getting ganged up on, hence the paralytic / snare weapons help the most.

The level design is very detailed and complex, to the point that you will get confused on where to go and what to do. Often they'll have you backtrack around, and you won't realize it until you're back in some main area. Everything looks the same, so it's hard to tell if you're seeing a new place or back where you started. The level design is so intricate you'll find yourself getting hung-up on walls and outcroppings while trying to back-peddle to retreat from enemies.

The plot starts semi-interestingly, but just kind of drifts off, as if whoever was writing it couldn't decide what direction to go. There's some semblance of an interesting game world out there, and you're only getting a very small sliver of it. But, it's introduced piece-meal in cut scenes. Little is explained, and your jerk main character is too busy being an a**hole to everyone he meets to care about listening to them explain things.

The main character is also a red x. It's hard to want to be him, because he's what a 12yo thinks "tough" should be; an insufferable a-hole that doesn't want to listen and "plays by his own rules". Meanwhile he's getting led around by the nose. This schtick worked for 80's action movie stars and Solid Snake, but the schtick has worn thin. There's a compelling world and events to be uncovered, and the main protagonist is doing everything they can to avoid you learning more about it.

Basically, whoever did the graphics in the game really busted their tail to optimize things. But, everything else about the game turns it into a "style over substance" endeavor. I really would like to recommend the game, but even the "just switch your brain off and treat it like a summer popcorn action movie" is stretching thin. By the time I was almost halfway through the game I just wanted it to be over, and just rushed through the rest to complete it. The enjoyment stops, and it feels like a chore. So, sadly, I have to give this a downvote.

*Hard Reset Redux*
----------------------------------------------
Por algum motivo, eu tive uma expectativa alta em cima desse jogo e acabei me frustrando com a repetitividade insana. Aqui temos um FPS Doom-like futurista e frenético, mas que sofre com cenários, inimigos e armas repetitivos demais.

Com a humanidade à beira da extinção por conta de uma guerra contra máquinas, o jogador se encontra na pele do Major Fletcher, um soldado que parte em uma jornada representando a última esperança da humanidade. Fletcher se vê no centro de um conflito que pode moldar o destino da humanidade, com muita ação intensa, dilemas morais e temas que já são de costume em histórias cyberpunk. Fletcher é um protagonista bem mediano, demonstrando muita frieza, desconfiança e sarcasmo em algumas situações.

O problema aqui é a estrutura linear demais, nos forçando a sempre estar fazendo as mesmas coisas: andar, matar robôs, apertar botões e matar mais robôs. Robôs estes que, apesar de terem suas diferenças, causam a impressão de que o jogador está enfrentando os mesmos inimigos desde o início do jogo. O jogo usa um conceito de poucas armas com upgrades, em vez de um arsenal variado, e você resolve quase tudo alternando entre os mesmos modos de tiro. A dificuldade não vem por conta de uma IA boa ou inimigos realmente desafiadores, mas sim pela quantidade de hordas que o jogo spamma na sua frente para tentar te matar.

Anda pra frente
Mata robô
Anda pra frente
Aperta botão
Mata robô

Isso é Hard Reset.

O jogo tem uma boa trilha sonora e uma ambientação que, apesar de repetitiva, é sim bem feita. Os gráficos são datados, a gameplay é direta, então, para quem curte Doom-like, em promoção, Hard Reset não é de se jogar fora.

Hard Reset is a perfect 5/10 experience, originally releasing in 2011 in the modern day the Redux plays similar to Doom. This does try and mix up the formula introducing enemies that react to limb shots, a focus on environmental damage and a weapon system where your guns transform rather than having several different weapons with some really nice animations.

However the charm eventually wears off with these enemies taking just 9 hours to beat it honestly felt twice as long as the enemies repeat, repeat and repeat. There are some new enemies introduced but it wasn't enough to make the gameplay feel fresh. There are even some boss fights but across the entire game I think the count is three. That's one boss fight every 3 hours.

Usually I can push past a lot of these irks in favour of the story but this game falls short on that for me also, mostly being told through comic book style cutscenes at the end of every mission it was very easy for me to skip or tune out a lot of the story.

Looping back this leaves us with a game I played for the gameplay for the most part and to summarize, the gameplay is fun but overstays it's welcome just a bit too much.

Запустела моя библиотека игр после закрытия гештальтов и я пошел искать новую игру. Долго думал покупать ли Shadow Warrior 3 и решил посмотреть, что ещё разработчики выпускали и тут появляется на глаза их первенец Hard Reset киберпанковый шутер. 

Обзоров на эту игру практически нет. А если и есть, то они бестолковые, и поэтому я решил, что нужно окунуться в это.

В целом не стал долго заморачиваться и запустил на сложном уровне сложности и получил вполне неплохой клон Doom’а в киберпанковом мире и врагами роботами.

На протяжении всех уровней расставлены взрывоопасные бочки и электрические щитки/генераторы, которые позволяют быстрее расправляться с противниками.
Пару раз за всю игру может быть несколько локаций из всех коридорных миссий, которые разнообразят шутерную составляющую по истреблению роботов и за это упадут достижения.

Враги тут губки, которые впитывают много урона, локации с боссами не вызывают «харда» и холодное оружие дают в середине и ты им никогда не воспользуешься.

В остальном игра очень красивая и сюжетик про небольшую историю товарища майора, точнее уже уволенного товарища майора в киберпанковой прослойке общества.

It's a shame that I have to give this game a negative review, even though it can be an average/decent time on normal difficulty there's a lot of things holding it back from being viscerally satisfying as a shooter, I'm convinced the devs didn't even playtest the harder difficulties because everything is so impossibly bullet  spongey it saps any fun that can be had out of the experience. Platforming and jumping is weird and floaty and doesn't feel good, many times leading to pitfalls and instant deaths. Enemies are too tanky for a shooter like this, similar to that Terminator game on Sega CD the enemies are all machinery and although it's interesting you can slightly dismember the large ones most of the time youll be emptying 80 bullets into 1 enemy hoping they'll finally die. 

The gunplay doesn't feel satisfying and most of the guns and upgrades feel worthless other than the RPG. The RPG tracking can be weird on aerial enemies frequently making you miss your shots not even by your fault. In a game that requires you to move constantly to stay alive the movement feels clunky, and there's too many uneven playing fields for you to get in a good movement flow, because you're constantly being stopped by textured objects in what should be flat arenas. The game designers have a totally inconsistent difficulty curve, some places it  seems they thought "We have run out of ideas so send wave after wave of bullet sponge enemies to overwhelm the player" I'm tired of every firefight being a boring 10 minute slog, an agonizing patience test, hope you don't get cheaply killed and saved halfway through every fight so you don't get cheated. There's no snap to the action, it's too hard and too slow paced to work as a visceral FPS game.

I'm 100% convinced that the devs didn't playtest Insanity difficulty it's an absolute slog, all the enemies are ultra bullet sponge tanky, I'm running out of ammo pickups half the time. The sword you get is completely useless on all difficulties too, so don't think about using that to save ammo. It is one of the least enjoyable high difficulty FPS playthroughs I've attempted in a long time, I've gotten to the junkyward stage and want to give a middle finger to the devs who designed this god awful level, just absolutely terrible level design, I heard these guys worked on Shadow Warrior (2013) and was excited to give it a shot but it's a mind numbing, frustrating, technically underwhelming experience with a shambled together incoherent storyline. I'd skip this one and go play old Shadow Warrior or the Shadow Warrior reboot, even Wolf 3D is better than this.

Hard Reset Redux, developed by Flying Wild Hog and published by Good Shepherd Entertainment, is a remastered edition of the 2011 cyberpunk-themed first-person shooter Hard Reset. Released in 2016, this redux version enhances the original with upgraded visuals, refined gameplay mechanics, and additional content, aiming to offer both newcomers and returning players a more polished and intense experience. It preserves the high-octane action and retro-shooter feel while modernizing the presentation to appeal to contemporary audiences.

The game is set in the dark, dystopian metropolis of Bezoar in the year 2436, where humanity faces extinction at the hands of rogue machines. Players step into the boots of Major Fletcher, a soldier tasked with defending the city’s last remaining strongholds against waves of hostile robots. The narrative unfolds through comic-book-style cutscenes and brief in-game dialogue, delivering a straightforward yet effective story that focuses on survival, heroism, and the high stakes of a society teetering on the edge of collapse. While the plot is not deeply complex, it provides a compelling backdrop for the relentless combat that defines the game.

Gameplay in Hard Reset Redux emphasizes fast-paced, tactical combat reminiscent of classic shooters. Players traverse linear, densely designed levels teeming with robotic enemies, each requiring attention to attack patterns and positioning. The game’s arsenal is notable for its versatility; the modular gun can switch between multiple firing modes, allowing players to adapt to different combat situations. In addition, the cyber-katana introduces a close-quarters option, adding variety to encounters. New movement mechanics, such as a dash ability, enhance mobility, enabling players to dodge attacks and reposition strategically during intense firefights. The combat loop is designed to be satisfying and visceral, rewarding quick reflexes and situational awareness.

Graphically, Hard Reset Redux represents a significant upgrade from the original. The new engine delivers detailed environments, improved lighting, and dynamic effects that give the cyberpunk city a vibrant, lived-in feel. The neon-lit streets, industrial interiors, and mechanized adversaries are all rendered with greater depth and clarity, enhancing immersion. The electronic soundtrack complements the visual style perfectly, creating an atmosphere of tension and urgency that drives the player forward through relentless battles.

Despite its strong presentation and engaging combat, the game has some limitations. Its linear level design can feel restrictive, lacking the exploratory freedom that some modern players expect. Additionally, the story serves more as a framework for action rather than a fully fleshed-out narrative, and the combat can become repetitive over longer sessions, as the core gameplay revolves around similar enemy encounters and patterns. While these aspects do not detract from the adrenaline-fueled action, they may limit the appeal for players seeking more variety or narrative depth.

Overall, Hard Reset Redux is a refined and exciting first-person shooter that successfully marries retro-inspired action with modern graphical enhancements. Its fast-paced combat, diverse arsenal, and immersive cyberpunk setting make it an engaging experience for fans of the genre. While it may not break new ground in storytelling or level design, it delivers a satisfying, visually striking, and action-packed journey that captures the essence of classic shooters for a modern audience.

Если учитывать, что оригинальная версия игры вышла в 2011 году и по скидке она стоит 71 рубль, то в целом — вполне неплохо.

Но если смотреть с точки зрения 2025 года, смысла в этой игре уже почти нет:

- Оружие ощущается неотзывчивым, иногда создаётся впечатление, что снаряды пролетают сквозь врагов или вовсе не наносят урона.
- Разнообразия противников мало.
- Игра довольно короткая, но из-за монотонности геймплея больше часа подряд в неё играть не хочется.
- Уровни построены по максимально однообразной схеме: зашёл в комнату — убил всех — нажал кнопку — снова зашёл в комнату... и так до самого конца.

Кат-сцены заслуживают отдельного упоминания. Я, честно говоря, никогда не видел настолько ужасного исполнения. Обычно в низкобюджетных играх это хотя бы красиво нарисованное слайд-шоу. Здесь же использованы какие-то уродливые, размазанные скетчи, вызывающие исключительно рвоту.

В общем, 10-14 лет назад, возможно, игра воспринималась нормально. Но сегодня она ощущается устаревшей и морально, и технически.

В целом, рецепт игры прост: киберпанк-окружение, линейные непродолжительные уровни, адекватное звуковое сопровождение (правда, разнообразием оно не блещет), подача "комунипофигистического" сюжета в виде комикса между миссиями и закадровым голосом во время миссии, незамысловато раскиданные секреты и... металлическое мяскО! Плюсом к этому идёт неплохая графика, даже с учётом возраста (и, прошу заметить, не осточертевшая новомодная пиксельная дичь), отсутствие фризов и вылетов на рабочий стол
   Для себя из минусов выделил бы слабый импакт от оружия и попаданий по врагам, некоторые дурацкие типы врагов (особенно бесят в определённых игровых сценах), присутствие багов коллизии героя с некоторыми игровыми объектами
   В итоге, довольно-таки крепкий старенький шутер на твёрдые 7/10. Если любите мясные шутаны и в своё время пропустили что оригинал, что переиздание "Redux", то рекомендую обратить внимание; а если по скидке, тогда брать обязательно!
